newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shippers fear rates rise on Schiphol nightflights.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shippers fear rates rise on Schiphol nightflights.

text.p: Dutch shippers fear a rates rise following the proposal that Schiphol airport will ban the take-off of some wide-body aircraft during the night time.

EVO, the Dutch shippers organisation, said in a statement shippers were "seriously concerned about the measures" and believe that the night ban will lead to a five to ten percent reduction in freight capacity.
Following this reduction, the EVO said it fears that rates will increase.
Schiphol has proposed a night take-off ban of the DC-10 and the Boeing 747 in its 100,200, 300 and SP versions. The Dutch government is expected to give its verdict on Schiphol's proposal this week.
Shippers believe "Schiphol's freight position will be eroded and the move will have a negative impact on the competitive position of the freight industry," in the long-term.
The group said that there will be great problems to find the right capacity, especially for over-size cargo and dangerous goods, the latter of which cannot go on passenger aircraft.
Schiphol estimated that 30,000 tonnes will be lost this year because of the ban, said the shippers, though they expect this to be a lot more.
EVO expects the night cargo to go to other Dutch airports, pushing more cargo on the roads, leading to further road congestion, it said.
The shippers are now calling for a meeting with the Minister of Transport.
